data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘aghal’ which means ‘to speak’ or ‘eloquent’. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that the name Aghala is a reminder of the importance of communication, both in speaking the truth and in listening to others with understanding and compassion. The name Aghala carries the meaning “The Eloquent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aghala usually hope their child will grow to embody the eloquent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Aghala was a Persian city located near the Caspian Sea, which was known for its strategic importance during the Sassanid Empire. It was a major port city and a center of trade between the East and the West. The city was captured by the Arab Muslim Army under the command of Al-Mansur during the Umayyad Caliphate in 731 AD.

historical_references.reference: Aghala was also the name of a Sufi saint from the 13th century in present-day Pakistan. He was a disciple of Sheikh Fariduddin Gangshir and is known for his poetry and spiritual teachings. The city of Agha Khan in Pakistan is named after him.
